doc.title: Pete Candoli interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 15, 1999

title: Boyd Raeburn's outside band at the Hurricane
summary: Pete describes Raeburn's large experimental band, its charts and personnel, and its wealthy backer.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing in Lionel Hampton's big band

blocks.x: Exactly. So finally with Woody’s band I was called, they had a Teen Time Show on NBC in California. It was called a Teen Time Show. It was on television. But before that I was with Boyd Raeburn’s band which was really outside. They had all real charts. We were going to open up — he had a backer for the band, Boyd did, and the band was a real outside band. George Handy was doing charts and people like that and they were going into a place called the Hurricane, which is right in Manhattan right near Nola Studios. And we were going to open up a supper club with Gertrude Nieson was the star of a show, and Boyd Raeburn was the band. And we had eight brass, Bernie Glow, Goz, me and Bernie Glow, Markie and some other trumpet. We had four rhythm and the mallet man, and the harp. In the woodwinds, we had seven woodwinds, which included bassoon, and also there was a tuba. And Ginny — not Ginny, I can’t think of her name it was Boyd Raeburn’s wife, she sang. But we were rehearsing, and while we were rehearsing at Nola’s, like Johnny Richards was writing, a wonderful writer for orchestra, really. And I remember we were receiving a check, I think I was getting $250 a week, but we weren’t doing anything because the club wasn’t finished. We were just rehearsing like a couple of

charts a week for about three weeks before we finally went in. And that was an excellent band. And Buddy DeFranco was on that band. And Boots was on that band, Boots Mussulli. And Leon Cox on trombone. Wonderful facility he had. I mean Dick Nole was another trombone player. Like Goz, and I can’t think Markie was there, Markowitz, and it was an excellent band. And we were there for about six weeks. And there was a man by the name of Stillman Pond, and his wife was really big in real estate, it was paying the whole payroll, which was — a backer.
Yeah. That’s a pretty large group to back too.
Yeah. Especially in those days, the backer is like, what?
